scene: Day 300, dusk at the edge of a huge grey gravel pit after days of rain. One whole side of the steep wall has slid down into a long slope of brown mud from the flooded floor to the rim, and thousands of green walkers are trudging up it out of the muddy water, past the half-sunk beige coach, toward the camera. In the foreground on the rim, Patch (white round head, orange bandage above his right eye, orange backpack) stumbles backward, eyes huge, one sweat drop, close to the camera, the waist-high metal barrier across the old road useless behind him. Tense because the place that held the horde now has a second way out.

Day 271, night at the depot gate. A thin torch beam cuts across the dark yard and stops on the small vent grille at the bottom of the wall; through the gate bars, three silhouettes stand in the street: a woman in a bright yellow raincoat with her fist raised to knock, a boy in a white bicycle helmet, and a big man with a blue and white checked blanket worn like a cape. In the foreground below ground, behind the grille, Patch (white round head, orange bandage above his right eye) stares up into the beam, eyes huge, one sweat drop, holding the orange backpack against his chest. Tense because strangers know exactly where he is hiding.
